ai_technology: AIROGS challenge winning deep-learning fundus-image classifier

evidence.ai_role: A learned image classifier supplied glaucoma scores used in external diagnostic evaluation.
evidence.tested: External existing-cohort diagnostic evaluation; not a prospective test of clinical benefit.
evidence.unknown: Clinical benefit and deployment outcomes are unestablished. The reported ROC-derived operating point is cohort-specific; prospective validation remains needed. Direct full-text access was blocked; bounded publisher-indexed Methods and Results were reviewed.

organization: The Rotterdam Eye Hospital; Erasmus Medical Center; Radboud University Medical Center; Institute of Molecular and Clinical Ophthalmology Basel

source_review.scope: Primary PubMed abstract/date/affiliations and publisher-indexed DL-algorithm-development, Validation dataset, participant ROC-threshold Results and Discussion passages. Direct publisher full-text fetch403; no full-PDF review claimed.

summary: An existing deep-learning fundus-image classifier was evaluated on 19,088 eyes from 9,837 Rotterdam Study participants, including 201 eyes with perimetric glaucoma. Eye-level sensitivity was 70.6% at 95% specificity, with ROC-AUC 0.911. Among 61 true positives with earlier images,33 were flagged before diagnosis. This retrospective evaluation of a prospectively collected cohort does not establish improved patient outcomes; image quality affected false positives. The reported specificity operating point was derived from this cohort’s ROC analysis, rather than a separately locked clinical cutoff.
title: AIROGS classifier detects glaucoma in retrospective Rotterdam validation
